#+title: Transparent build-station production

Run the normal commands:

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl build
./bin/bl build --force
./bin/bl self-build --out ./bl-release
#+end_src

Managed preparation uses Nix's configured remote builders. The daemon owns
transport and credentials; each command uses the same policy. A missing or
unreachable builder produces a preparation error and preserves the selection.

The workstation's existing host configuration is
hosts/work/remote-build.nix in the workstation repository. It configures
ssh-ng, the station's public host key and the daemon-owned private key location.
The installed machine list is /etc/nix/machines.

For a managed host using this repository's module, supply a local build
description to the module factory. Addresses, credentials, host keys and
capacity belong to the workstation repository, outside Beam Lisp:

#+begin_src nix
imports = [ (beam-lisp.lib.artifact-workstation {
  station = import ./local-build-station.nix;
}) ];
#+end_src

The local description supplies hostName, sshUser, sshKey, systems, maxJobs,
supportedFeatures and optionally hostPublicKey. The private key remains a
host file; its bytes must never enter the Nix store. Deploy through the host's
normal administration workflow once. The factory disables local production.

Remote Nix builders place realization on the station. They do not place Nix
evaluation there. Moving evaluation requires an operator-provided endpoint
with that capability; an ssh-ng store credential alone cannot run commands.

Generic hosts can use nixosModules.artifacts and set
services.beam-lisp-artifacts.buildStation. A null station keeps the host's
local builder role. Station daemon/worker resource limits are configured on
the station itself; client limits describe a separate execution domain.

The existing nixosModules.artifact-workstation export remains a module, but
now requires services.beam-lisp-artifacts.buildStation from local data. It
refuses a missing station rather than silently enabling builds on Work.

* Optional evaluation placement

A local description can additionally supply =evaluation=:

#+begin_src nix
evaluation = {
  storeUri = "ssh-ng://builder@build.example.invalid";
  transport = [ "ssh" "operator@build.example.invalid" "{endpoint}" ];
};
#+end_src

These are examples, not Beam Lisp defaults. The local operator owns addresses,
credentials and SSH host-key policy. The transport must permit running the
immutable endpoint sent with the platform. An existing forced ssh-ng key does
not grant that capability. Leave evaluation null for a store-only station.
The client copies the platform and captured inputs, invokes its finite recipe
endpoint, copies the result back and retains it before acknowledging remote
root cleanup. A configured endpoint failure never falls back to Work.

The NixOS module emits this local description as
=/etc/beam-lisp/build-station.json=. It is host configuration, never project
input or a field in an artifact request. No resident service is required.
Unacknowledged outputs remain rooted under the station user's
=$XDG_CACHE_HOME/beam_lisp/station/TICKET= for recovery. Each request has its own
root, including concurrent requests for identical products.

Source capture still reads the local checkout. Bootstrap coordinator selection
also remains local. The endpoint moves the SDK, native, application and portable
product's actual recipe evaluation and realization to the station. This slice
does not claim that the current store-only workstation credential has been
upgraded or that its host deployment has been activated.
